walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

A noun phrase is a sentence that contains nouns.
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
A syntactic unit headed by a noun, which may include determiners, adjectives and modifiers — e.g. 'the big red car' is a noun phrase functioning as a single grammatical unit.
A noun phrase is just a noun by itself.
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
Register is the same as accent.
Register is just how loud you speak.
A variety of language used in a particular social setting — varying by formality, field (topic) and mode (spoken/written) to suit audience and purpose.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between inflectional and derivational morphology?
options: Register is the same as accent.
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
Inflection and derivation are two words for the same process.

Inflectional morphemes mark grammatical features without changing word class (cat/cats, walk/walked); derivational morphemes create new words, often changing word class (happy → happiness, teach → teacher).
